goal.summary: Diagnosed from his app.log: 44/44 models.cubric.studio downloads failed in under 200ms while 45/45 github.com downloads succeeded. His ISP intercepts the connection. He is unblocked TODAY by running Cloudflare WARP for the whole download - he verified a plain DNS switch is NOT enough and that the stream dies mid-transfer at about 20 percent, which means deep-packet interference rather than hostname blocking. Four app defects the log exposed are fixed and committed as 6b27ab4b, version stamped 1.3.1, notes approved, 71/71 suites green.

next_action.description: Decide the mirror. Everything else in 1.3.1 is done. The app-side failover is built, tested and inert; it needs ONE origin added to _MODEL_MIRRORS in routes/downloadManager.js to go live, and no further app change after that if the origin is added before v1.3.1 ships. Cheapest first step is a second custom domain on the existing cubric-models R2 bucket - free, since it is one bucket with no duplicate storage, R2 egress is free, and custom domains carry no per-domain charge. But it is same-provider and UNPROVEN against the deep-packet interference this user hit. If it fails his test, move to an off-Cloudflare origin: GitHub Releases (proven to reach this exact user in his own log; the 2GB per-asset cap forces splitting the big transformers), Hugging Face, or Backblaze B2.

key_decisions: The transition TABLE was deliberately NOT widened to allow failed to queued. Widening it would also license the reconciler to resurrect a settled job, which invariant #3 forbids. requeueDep is a side door for user-driven retry only, and a test asserts the table still refuses the transition.

_MODEL_MIRRORS ships EMPTY on purpose. Failing over to a host that does not exist turns one clean error into two slow ones. CUBRIC_MODEL_MIRRORS, comma-separated origins, overrides it for testing without a rebuild.

The marker-url comparison had to become path-equal BEFORE failover could be safe. MPI-317 deleted the partial on a url mismatch, so a host swap would have scrapped exactly the bytes failover exists to preserve. The SHA256 verify remains the net.
Remote and Pod requeues still zero downloadedBytes, correctly - there is no local partial there. Only the two LOCAL requeue sites credit getPartialBytes().

An earlier reading of this incident - that Cloudflare itself was blocked - was WRONG and briefly went to the user as advice. He later confirmed Cloudflare WORKS and it is his current workaround. Read the whole exchange in brief.md before re-deriving anything about Cloudflare.
